station.title: Step 1 of 5 — your station

form.title: Step 4 of 5 — server settings
form.description:
{image}

Fill the form in, then press **Save**.

**URL**
{urls}
Without `http://` or `https://`. Use an address your station can reach on your own network — there is no reason to expose Home Assistant to the internet for this. If your station cannot resolve names, use the IP address.

**Station ID** — anything you like. It becomes the device name in Home Assistant.

**Station key** — {key_hint}.

**Upload interval** — 1 minute is a good default.

**API type** — *WSLink API*. Pick *WUnderground API* only if your station does not offer WSLink: it carries half as many readings and only four channels.

**Upload** — leave it enabled.

> ⏱️ Some stations drop off Wi-Fi if you linger on this screen. Have the address ready, fill it in, and save.

confirm.title: Step 5 of 5 — confirm & exit
confirm.description:
{image}

Go back, then press **Confirm & Exit**.

> ⚠️ **Confirm & Exit is what writes the settings to the station.** Saving alone changes nothing.

Press Next once you have.

invalid_station_key.title: Weather station rejected: wrong station key
invalid_station_key.description:
A weather station at {ip} tried to send data as `{station_id}` but did not send the expected station key.

Check that the station key configured in the station or in the WSLink app matches the one set in this integration. This message disappears on its own once a request from {ip} is accepted.

missing_device_id.title: Weather station rejected: no station identifier
missing_device_id.description:
A weather station at {ip} sent data without a station identifier.

Set a Sender ID in the WSLink app, or an ID parameter in the station configuration. This message disappears on its own once a request from {ip} is accepted.

legacy_entity_ids.title: Entity IDs repeat the station name

confirm.title: Shorten the entity IDs
confirm.description:
Up to version 1.0.8 this integration built entity IDs that carry the station name twice, such as `{example_old}`. New stations no longer do.

**{count} entities** can be renamed, for example to `{example_new}`.

History and long-term statistics follow the rename automatically. **Automations, scripts, scenes and dashboards do not** — you will have to update anything that refers to the old IDs yourself.

If you would rather keep them as they are, ignore this repair.

legacy_status_sensors.title: Connection, leak and battery readings are still numbers

confirm.title: Convert to binary sensors
confirm.description:
Connection, water leak and battery readings are reported as 1 or 0. Up to version 1.0.8 they were exposed as numeric sensors, such as `{example}`, which cannot be used with the standard leak, connectivity and low-battery cards of Home Assistant. New stations get binary sensors showing **Wet / Dry**, **Connected / Disconnected** and **On / Off**.

**{count} entities** can be converted. The 0~5 battery levels of the air quality sensors keep their percentage: six steps are more than an on/off can carry.

Changing platform is not a rename, so the old entities are removed and rebuilt as `binary_sensor`. **Their recorded history is lost** — these readings have no long-term statistics, so only the raw history is affected — and **automations, scripts, scenes and dashboards pointing at them must be updated**. The new entities appear on the station's next upload.

If you would rather keep them as they are, ignore this repair.

no_station_yet.title: No weather station has sent anything yet

confirm.title: Set up your weather station
confirm.description:
Your weather station creates the devices and sensors — there is nothing to add here.

In the station's app, open your station, then **Settings → Weather server → Other Server**, and fill in:

**URL**
{urls}
Without `http://` or `https://`. Use an address your station can reach on your own network — there is no reason to expose Home Assistant to the internet for this. If your station cannot resolve names, use the IP address.

**Station ID** — anything you like. It becomes the device name in Home Assistant.

**Station key** — {key_hint}.

**Upload interval** — 1 minute is a good default.

**API type** — *WSLink API*.

**Upload** — leave it enabled.

Press **Save**, go back, then press **Confirm & Exit**.

> ⚠️ **Confirm & Exit is what writes the settings to the station.** Saving alone changes nothing. Your sensors appear a second after you press it.

The endpoints listening for uploads are:
{endpoints}

received.title: Your station is through
received.description:
**{station}** has sent its first upload. Its sensors are being created now, and more appear as the station reports them.

This message will not come back.

timeout.title: Nothing received yet
timeout.description:
No upload arrived in {minutes} minutes.

In order of likelihood:

  - **Did you press Confirm & Exit?** Saving the server screen alone does not write anything to the station.
  - The **URL** has to be {urls_inline}, without `http://`, and reachable by the station on your network.
  - **Upload** must be enabled on that screen.
  - Some Bresser firmwares from **3.02** onwards refuse plain HTTP and need an address serving HTTPS.
  - The upload interval may simply be longer than the wait.
  - **Station key**: {key_hint}.

If the station reached Home Assistant but was turned away, it is reported separately in **Settings → System → Repairs**.

You can close this. It stays here until a station shows up, and reopening it starts the wait again.

progress.waiting_for_station: Waiting for your station's first upload…

abort.not_received: Nothing has arrived yet, so this is left open. It stays in Repairs until a station shows up, and you can reopen it to wait again.

unknown_parameters.title: Station {station} is sending readings that are being dropped
unknown_parameters.description:
**{count} parameters** from **{station}** are not recognised, so their values are discarded on every upload:

{parameters}

The usual cause is a station reporting more than its protocol can carry. Weather Underground has only **4 slots** for extra sensors; if your station offers **WSLink** as an *API type*, switching to it exposes seven channels and roughly twice as many readings.

If that is not it, these parameter names are exactly what a bug report needs: open one on the [issue tracker]({issue_tracker}) and they can be added.

You can also ignore this — nothing is broken, these particular values simply do not arrive.

no_wind_direction.message: Station {device} has not reported a wind direction yet, so there is nothing to calibrate against. Wait for the next upload and try again.
